claims: The requirement for Selective Service registration applies to male citizens and residents aged 18 through 25.
Registration for Selective Service must occur within 30 days of turning 18.
The Selective Service registration obligation lasts until the 26th birthday.
There is currently no active U.S. military draft.
Nearly all male U.S. citizens and male immigrants (documented or undocumented) living in the U.S. who are 18-25 must register for Selective Service.
Late registration for Selective Service is accepted up to age 26.
Men currently on full-time active duty in the armed forces are excepted from Selective Service registration.
Students in service academies are excepted from Selective Service registration.
Men with disabilities that keep them confined to a residence or hospital are excepted from Selective Service registration.
Failure to register for Selective Service is a felony.
Failure to register for Selective Service can lead to losing eligibility for federal student loans.
Failure to register for Selective Service can lead to losing eligibility for federal grants.
Failure to register for Selective Service can lead to losing eligibility for federal job training.
Failure to register for Selective Service can lead to losing eligibility for federal employment.
Under current law, women are not required to register for Selective Service.
As of April 2026, the U.S. Army allows new recruits to enlist between 17 and 42.
Parental permission is required for 17-year-olds to enlist in the U.S. Army.
If a draft were activated, Congress and the President would decide the specific age parameters.
U.S. military draft age parameters have historically focused on men aged 18-25.
